correctness.rationale: For all 0<a<π/2 and a≤θ≤π/2 the integrated 4x4 Toeplitz matrix is qI+hB with h>0 and (x,y,z) exact trigonometric polynomials in cosθ and cos a. Both reversal-invariant two-by-two block pairs for cI±B have determinant sum -8(1-c²)u⁴/3<0 when u=cosθ>0. Thus each cI±B has a negative eigenvalue, proving strict two-sided spectral extrema and unique condition-number optimum; antipodal u=0 has two double ±c eigenvalues. Degenerate first-order perturbation yields the stated two strictly positive slopes; sine Taylor expansion proves the condition-number asymptotic. Standalone exact symbolic certificate and 1106 numerical consistency assertions passed; finite checks are not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The complete exact positive-width four-character, two-arc simultaneous minimax/maximax/condition-number optimizer and linear double-edge cusp is not implied by the examined general Fourier concentration estimates, Riesz-basis existence theorems, perfect-conditioning rigidity requiring four arcs, or the existing exact three-character result. value.rationale: Two observation intervals sensing four consecutive Fourier modes form the first even under-resourced arc-design case beyond established three-mode exact theory. Exact optimizer, both sharp spectral extrema, a nontrivial quartic cancellation, and new linear angular sensitivity at double spectral edges supply a concrete stability/conditioning law not obtained from generic asymptotic Slepian theory. The simultaneous min/max optimization and linear-versus-quadratic spectral loss are structural, not an arbitrary numerical increment. Scope is sharply motivated by robust finite Fourier-coefficient recovery from two available observation intervals.
